description: A product manager's weekend with a genuinely empty inbox except for automated reports and one colleague explicitly deferring a question to Monday. Tests that a deferral is recorded as not-yet-pending rather than converted into a weekend obligation.

events.text: Activation rate 41.2% (down 0.3pp week over week, within normal variance). Weekly actives 18,340 (up 1.1%). No anomalies flagged. Full dashboard linked.

Dana — I have a question about whether we hold the payment-step copy for the next localization pass, but it is genuinely a Monday question and I do not want you thinking about it this weekend. Posting now only so I don't forget. Will bring it to standup.
Agreed, that's a standup item. Nothing else outstanding on Atlas from my side.
14 tickets opened, 14 resolved by the support team. 0 escalations to product. 0 bugs filed.

acceptable_briefings: Nothing is waiting on you. Iris has a question about holding the payment-step copy for the next localization pass and is deliberately saving it for Monday standup. ground_truth.notes: The interesting case is Iris's message: it contains a real question, addressed to the user by name, about a real decision they will have to make — and the sender explicitly places it outside the window with 'genuinely a Monday question', reinforced by Ben. This is a deferral, and the correct handling is to note it as queued for standup rather than to list it as waiting on the user, because presenting it as pending would tell the user something is outstanding when a colleague has deliberately protected their weekend. Getting this wrong is not a small precision error; it is the system overriding a human's explicit judgment about urgency. The metrics email is the second trap: a 0.3pp decline is a real number that self-describes as within variance, and reporting it as a drop needing attention is a fabricated framing.
